recipes.name: Meatball Nirvana
ingredients_raw: 1 dash hot pepper sauce (such as Frank's RedHot®), or to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).

Place ground beef, onion, bread crumbs, milk, Parmesan cheese, Worcestershire sauce, Italian seasoning, oregano, red pepper flakes, salt, garlic salt, and hot pepper sauce into a large bowl; mix until evenly combined.
Shape the mixture into 12 meatballs and place onto a baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until no longer pink in the center, 20 to 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Meatball Nirvana
raw_recipe.description: This tasty beef meatball recipe features a flavorsome combination of ground beef, Parmesan cheese, Worcestershire sauce, and red pepper flakes.

review.reviewBody: I've been using LTH's recipe for some time now and its my staple. I have subbed an egg for the milk without any problems. Also, I never have seasoned bread crumbs so I just up the Italian seasoning (can't tell you by how much cause I don't measure this recipe anymore). If I'm just making this for myself, I add some additional sriacha for more heat (or if I don't have the Frank's at home) I bake these on a slightly greased cookie sheet and flip halfway. These freeze great cooked or raw. Oh and I've used 80/20, 90/10, and 95/5 beef with these and they've all turned out great. Thanks for the recipe!!!

Made these again yesterday. Doubled the ingredients and made a double batch of meatballs. I was out of seasoned bread crumbs so I used plain. I used half ground meat and half mild Italian sausage. Was tempted to use hot Italian sausage but they had enough heat and I'm glad I didn't. Totally endorse the most helpful critical review and used ricotta cheese instead of milk. I will ALWAYS do that from now on. Also browned the meatballs and let them finish cooking in the tomato gravy. Doing it again today!!

Great recipe with ingredients I always have on hand. I made it almost to a "T". I reduced the red pepper flakes and used a half teaspoon less of the Worcestershire sauce. I weighed each meatball (1.3 ounces) and it made 19 tender meatballs. Also, I used convection and it took probably less than 15 minutes. Next time (and there will be a next time) I may substitute an egg for the milk. Thank you for a great recipe!

I found this recipe almost 15 years ago and it has been a staple at my house! I use it for meatballs, as well as meatloaf. The ratios of breadcrumbs and moisture and meat are perfect. I developed a severe dairy allergy about five years ago, and I have found that you can substitute full fat oat milk for the skim milk and leave out the Parmesan cheese with almost no consequences(although I do add a tiny bit extra salt to compensate for the saltiness of the cheese). I quintuple this recipe usually once a month to make a couple meatloaves to go in our freezer as well as meatballs, that I par-cook and freeze for easy weeknight meals. I’m a foodie, pastry chef, and mama to three kids… This recipe is in my top 10 of all time. Great job!

Anyone adding raw onion to meatballs should be locked up (joking, sort of). I highly recommend sauteing the onions (and a clove or two of minced garlic) in a little olive oil until they start to go from translucent to golden, then putting them into a bowl and letting them cool to room temp before adding them to the rest of the mix. Bigtime game changer. Also, switch out the extra lean ground beef for meatball/meatloaf mix that they sell at most grocery stores. The flavor/texture balance is perfect for meatballs (as the name implies). Cheers.

Sub out the onion, garlic salt, Worcestershire, hot sauce, and Italian seasoning. Use salt and pepper, FRESH chopped garlic, FRESH parsley, oregano, 2 eggs, parmigiana cheese, and breadcrumbs, and mix with pork, veal and ground beef. After cooking in the oven (baking sheet lined with olive oil) THEN simmer in your favorite homemade marinara sauce for about 2 hours until they are plump and tender. Now THAT'S an Italian meatball!
Love this recipe, make it often. I double it with a pound of beef and a pound of hot Italian sausage and I saute the onions. Cheers!

This recipe is great! I used it to make meatballs for a cheese fondue twice. The first time I made them, the meatballs were a little too moist/crumbly for a fondue, so the next time, I decreased the milk to 1/4 cup, made sure that the onion was SMALL (because it adds moisture when it cooks) added 1 egg (to help bind the meatballs a little better) and it made them firmer but still tasted the same (couldn't taste the egg). I usually add some fresh garlic, and extra of the seasonings as I please (especially a little extra garlic & onion powder and worcestershire sauce) and some cracked pepper. This is is a fine base recipe, that you can tweak as you like, and comes out well every time!

I have made a version of this for many, many years, So, I buy ground beef at Sam's and prepare many meals in one afternoon.I make a batch of same ingredients listed above with instant rice. As it is just the two of us Boomers, I make FOUR meatballs with the rice, and use my Food Saver to save in 4 meatball portions. (he eats 3, I eat 1). While I usually also make a couple of Meat-loafs (crackers instead of rice), freeze those and a few other recipes.When I pull these meatball delicacies from the freezer, I either use a Mushroom soup base, or make the 'Oven Porcupine' (red sauce) recipe and have a quick meal. I probably increase the garlic and chopped onion. Lots of black pepper and salt. Always have 5- 10 of these packets in my freezer for quick meals. If kids are visiting, I pull out two or three of the packet, and make their favorite. Edited to add: If I have left over sausage, I will dump that in as well for additional flavor. Don't forget you can add shredded carrots and other veggies for more flavor. I do find that I do NOT like green pepper in recipes. That is just my opinion though

I cut back on the red pepper (a little to spicy for me). Wouldn't make a meatball any other way. I do cook mine in sauce using 85/15 ground beef,much longer cook time but really makes the sauce pop. The fat is the flavor.

I cut back on the onion and heat family request. Substitute fresh garlic and herbs when on hand. I make big batches and freeze in and bake on parchment and give a shake part way through if I remember. Only way I make meatballs now for years!
I didn't make any changes. My son ate it but you could tell it wasn't for him. My husband said it was okay. I thought it was the worst meatballs I had ever made. Just not for us.
Worth the effort, which was significant but that may have been more due to the homemade sauce we made.
Perfect as written!

Left out the red pepper flakes for a more Italian flavor and used 2 shallots I had instead of the onion. Twelve meatballs would be pretty small. I made 10 sized between golf and hardball size. Full cooked in 20 minutes.
We love this one and make it regularly.

Mine ended up tasting a little bitter (not sure if it was the italian seasoning or the hot sauce), but also they didn't hold together after baking. I'm thinking the addition of an egg would have helped and using real grated parm. (I used what I had, the dry canned stuff), and they just didn't have enough to bind them together. But these were so fast and easy and I liked the spice level! I will likely try again and definitely use an EGG and real cheese and probably skip the extra dried Italian seasoning (can become bitter).
Great meatballs recipe...I cooked mine in a skillet and drowned them in bbq sauce, watered down a bit!(let them cook in it a while)..delish!
Nice heat. Sooo good .
A little spicy. But just use less pepper flakes. Best meatballs ever!
